mathematical_scope: 8 unittest methods covering tree shapes, modular Cayley action against a dense inverse, modular mixer round trips, small full inverse matrices, alpha=2 root-leaf formula, graph edges, numeric unitarity/cuts and one-stage Fourier falsification. The dense inverse helper uses modular Gauss–Jordan; the vector helper uses zip and assumes matching dimensions.
input_and_guard_coverage: Selected valid sizes/seeds only. NumPy-dependent tests deliberately skip if importing NumPy fails. Invalid parent arrays, singular modular pivots, malformed vector lengths, wrong modulus and alternate alpha are not comprehensively tested. Zero-length/square-matrix guards are absent in test helpers.
cost_and_scaling: Dense inversion/cross-products are cubic in small N; full inverse tests use N8,16, numerical SVD N32..128. Tree tests cover depth9 (1023 vertices) but are not all-depth proof.
test_evidence: All 8 tests precede unittest.main and are visible to direct/discovery runs. Two can be skipped while the unittest run exits 0 and says Ran 8 tests; validate.py would still label all8 passed. No tests run here.
dependency_identity: Assigned audit.py b2858676a50b… plus unitary_mixer hash-only identity aff6a16c…. NumPy optional in two tests and version unpinned.

findings.finding: Two substantive tests are optional via skipTest. Any downstream suite summary must distinguish skipped from passed; validate.py currently does not. Globally absent NumPy would also break its later mandatory numerical probe, so absent NumPy alone does not imply the entire driver can finish successfully.
Dense independent algebraic formulations are useful controls but depend on the same field/modulus and constructor; their presence is not evidence that the archived tests were executed.

acceptance_boundary: Accept source-level test specification, with 8 discovered methods and possible skips. No pass count or dependency-body coverage is inferred.
